title: Lifecycle-based risk management for business AI use
text: Adopt voluntary risk management practices across the AI lifecycle and continuously update countermeasures. Define risks, mitigations, and review cadence with owners. Treat this as a maintained governance practice rather than a one-time document.

title: Governance structure and accountability for AI use
text: Define governance roles, responsibilities, and decision processes for AI use in business operations. Require decision logs for risk acceptance and exceptions. Governance should enable internal explainability: ‘who approved what and why’.

framework: AI Governance Guidelines (Implementation of AI Principles)
title: Agile governance and continuous updates
text: Use agile governance to continuously update controls as deployments and risks evolve. Define lightweight but repeatable review cycles and escalation rules. The objective is rapid learning and explainable adjustments, not bureaucratic delay.

framework: APPI (Act on the Protection of Personal Information)
title: Purpose specification and appropriate handling of personal information
text: Handle personal information under defined principles and align processing with appropriate purposes. For AI chatbots, define purposes for data collection, logging, analytics, and training (if any). Maintain documentation so purpose boundaries are explainable to stakeholders and regulators.

title: Security safeguards for personal information
text: Implement safeguards to prevent leakage, loss, and unauthorized access to personal information. For AI systems, include access control for logs/embeddings, monitoring, and incident handling. Security controls should map to plausible abuse scenarios and be maintained as evidence.

title: Transparency and stakeholder communication
text: Provide appropriate transparency about AI use, limitations, and risks to stakeholders. For customer-facing chatbots, disclose AI involvement and define escalation routes to humans. Transparency is part of trust and reduces misuse and overreliance.

title: Human oversight for high-impact use cases
text: Ensure oversight mechanisms exist for higher-risk contexts and harm scenarios. Define when human review is required and how interventions are logged. Operational oversight is a core ingredient for explainable governance and incident investigation.

title: Socio-technical governance framing for AI systems
text: Treat AI governance as management of socio-technical risks across systems, services, stakeholders, and lifecycle changes. Governance should cover technical controls, operational processes, and stakeholder communication. The goal is explainability under uncertainty and change.

title: Individual rights and oversight expectations
text: Maintain processes to respect individual rights and appropriate handling of personal information. Ensure that logs and records can support access/correction requests without leaking others’ data. Rights handling should be operationally feasible and documented.

title: Regulator expectations and compliance tracking
text: Track PPC publications and regulator expectations and align governance controls accordingly. Keep a lightweight change log of new guidance and how internal controls were updated. This supports explainable compliance posture rather than reactive firefighting.
